application_review: PROGRESS. The preceding projection-compatibility round was rechecked before edits. Retained proof source hashes and axiom sets remain unchanged.

The first-order mixed cube has one nonroot vertex. Reindexing its increment gives exactly subgroup Haar averaging. Haar invariance passes through the actual convex hull, and a unit invariant function is itself a mixed-dual generator.

The first-order Hilbert projection is identified using actual Haar self-adjointness. Its residual has zero weighted pairing against every invariant generator, hence against the closed span. The input needs only a uniform L2 bound when its Haar output is already represented by a unit-hull family.

For actual unit inputs, original normalized nonnegative cell weights provide a bounded actual Haar representative, still unit bounded, whose Hilbert image is exactly the first-order projection. No diagonalization or tail-containing-ultrafilter hypothesis is required.

Subgroup inclusion gives the antitone inclusion of the first-order closed spaces: larger-subgroup invariant generators are also invariant under the smaller subgroup. Span and topological closure preserve this inclusion.

For a first-subgroup unit generator, its second-subgroup projection is the actual Haar average. The exact composition identity and the first invariance identify it with the sum-subgroup Haar average, placing it in the sum-subgroup generator set.

Continuity makes the inverse image of the sum space under the second projection closed. Thus the generator result extends to the entire first closed space. Vectors in the intersection are fixed by the second projection, proving the base concatenation containment. Antitone inclusions provide the reverse containment and hence equality.

Eight theorems are audited. This proves the actual first-order base case of the concatenation induction, not the higher-degree containment at degree d1+d2-1 or the full qualitative Bessel theorem. The original main target remains unproved.
remaining: The common-system master estimates, first-order Bessel, dual energy reduction, recursion and stability are proved. Actual dual functions now have a common finite empirical approximation preserving arbitrary cell probabilities, unit bounds and uniform bounded-test correlations. Exact arbitrary-vertex reflection of the actual subgroup cube law and mixed products is now proved. Mixed cubes now have exact arbitrary-vertex duality and weighted single-vertex replacement estimates. Finite products of dual functions now have quantitative empirical approximation uniform over bounded tests. Exact translated-product expansions and extraction for each fixed test are now proved. The exact mixed face split, projected-face correlation and one-step face Cauchy-Schwarz inequality are now proved. Face energies are now identified with actual copied cube means, with nonnegativity and copy algebra verified. Arbitrary-coordinate permutation invariance, copied-mean nonnegativity and reflection bounds are now established. Full multidimensional mixed Gowers Cauchy-Schwarz, the product-root bound and the single-vertex bound are now proved. Actual dual anti-uniformity, its weighted version and the finite zero-root orthogonality characterization are now proved. Mixed dual recursion, covariance and exact subgroup-shift expansions are now established. Same-subgroup mixed-dual finite products now have an exact averaged dual representation and retain weighted anti-uniformity. The actual unit-input mixed-dual convex hull now has multiplicative and translation closure with unchanged weighted anti-uniform bounds. For varying finite groups and cell types, the exact weighted Haar Hilbert realization and vanishing-Gowers/closed-dual-span orthogonality equivalence are now proved. The dual Hilbert span now has uniformly bounded scaled-hull representatives dense in its closure; their bound may depend on the approximation. Fixed-polynomial and continuous functional calculus for scaled-hull representatives, their clipping closure, and unit-interval-valued approximation of the actual dual Hilbert projection are now proved. The actual dual projection now controls the limiting Gowers power and yields unit-interval models with arbitrarily small Gowers error along the same ultrafilter. For ultrafilters containing every tail, diagonalization now provides one exact unit-interval representative of the dual projection and residual Gowers convergence to zero. Actual unit mixed-dual-hull multiplication now preserves the closed dual space and its orthogonal complement and satisfies the genuine projection pull-out identity on represented inputs. Every unit-bounded actual representative in the closed mixed-dual subspace now multiplies that subspace and its orthogonal complement into themselves. The genuine projection pull-out identity extends to these structured multipliers without requiring cellwise convex-hull membership. Actual translations, with shifts allowed to vary by stage and cell, act linearly on weighted-Haar L2-bounded families, preserve their Hilbert distances, and have inverse-shift adjoints. They preserve the closed mixed-dual subspace and its orthogonal complement; the genuine dual projection commutes with translation on actual represented inputs. Closed Hilbert subspaces containing every selected actual unit family now contain their internal finite averages, using fixed sample counts and the original weighted L2 variance bound. Finite products of unit represented structured inputs remain structured. Taking a mixed dual along any second subgroup system preserves the first closed dual space for such inputs. A unit represented member of the first space orthogonal to the intersection has vanishing second-system Gowers seminorm and is orthogonal to the entire second dual space. For tail-containing ultrafilters and positive degrees, actual dual projections now preserve the other closed dual space and commute on the entire completed Hilbert space. The proof first transfers orthogonality using actual unit-bounded projection representatives, proves unit-interval compatibility and an exact intersection model, then extends closed-space preservation from bounded generators by projection continuity and derives full commutation by self-adjointness. The first-order mixed dual is now identified with actual subgroup Haar averaging. Its unit hull consists of subgroup-invariant functions, and unit invariant functions belong to it. Actual first-order projections have exact unit Haar representatives. The first-order closed dual space is antitone in the subgroup, and its base concatenation is proved as the full equality of the two first-order spaces intersection with the first-order space of the subgroup sum, for every ultrafilter. Higher-order concatenation controlling dual correlations and the full qualitative Bessel theorem remain missing, as do remaining replica integration, cyclic-to-interval transfer and inverse correlator existence. Coloring-derived targets, Calibration/Alignment and final ordered positive rapidly separated monochromatic extraction remain. StrongConjecture is unchanged and unproved. No unavoidable blocker is established; publication, PR and prize application remain pending.
